questions.prompt: At Rome the wise consul, when the news had been heard, stayed at home.
questions.answer: Rōmae cōnsul sapiēns, nūntiō audītō, domī mānsit.

questions.prompt: Yesterday at Corinth the merchants sold much grain.
questions.answer: Herī Corinthī mercātōrēs multum frūmentum vēndidērunt.

questions.prompt: Born at Rhodes, the famous orator used to teach at Athens.
questions.answer: Rhodī nātus, ōrātor clārus Athēnīs docēbat.

questions.prompt: At Brundisium the fleet, held back by a storm, was idle for many days.
questions.answer: Brundisiī classis, tempestāte retenta, per multōs diēs cessāvit.

questions.prompt: Remaining at home, the sick old man thought much about death.
questions.answer: Domī manēns, senex aegrōtus multa dē morte cōgitābat.

questions.prompt: The wounded soldier, stretched on the ground, kept begging for help.
questions.answer: Mīles vulnerātus humī prōstrātus auxilium implōrābat.

questions.prompt: Living in the country, the diligent farmer never rested.
questions.answer: Rūrī vīvēns, agricola dīligēns numquam cessābat.

questions.prompt: In suspense of mind, the mother anxiously awaited her son's return.
questions.answer: Animī pendēns, māter reditum fīliī anxiē exspectābat.

questions.prompt: At Delphi the oracle, consulted by many, often seemed obscure.
questions.answer: Delphīs ōrāculum, ā multīs cōnsultum, obscūrum saepe vidēbātur.

questions.prompt: At Corinth the rich merchant, though old, was still energetic.
questions.answer: Corinthī mercātor dīves, quamquam senex, adhūc impiger erat.

questions.prompt: At Ephesus the temple of Diana, praised by all, was held most beautiful.
questions.answer: Ephesī templum Diānae, ab omnibus laudātum, pulcherrimum habēbātur.

questions.prompt: Studying at Athens, the young Roman admired the wisdom of the Greeks.
questions.answer: Athēnīs studēns, iuvenis Rōmānus sapientiam Graecōrum admīrābātur.

questions.prompt: Left at home, the little boy wept for his absent mother.
questions.answer: Domī relictus, puer parvus mātrem absentem flēbat.

questions.prompt: In the evening, in the country, the master dismissed the laborers worn out by toil.
questions.answer: Vesperī rūrī dominus operāriōs labōre dēfessōs dīmīsit.

questions.prompt: Yesterday, sitting on the ground, the wretched beggar sought alms from passers-by.
questions.answer: Herī humī sedēns, mendīcus miser stīpem ā praetereuntibus petēbat.

questions.prompt: Living at Rhodes, the poor philosopher cultivated temperance more than riches.
questions.answer: Rhodī habitāns, philosophus pauper temperantiam magis quam dīvitiās colēbat.

questions.prompt: At Carthage the most beautiful queen, seized by love, welcomed the Trojan guest.
questions.answer: Carthāginī rēgīna pulcherrima, amōre capta, hospitem Trōiānum excēpit.

questions.prompt: Anxious in mind, the fearful citizens awaited news about the war.
questions.answer: Animī pendentēs, cīvēs nūntium dē bellō trepidī opperiēbantur.

questions.prompt: At Athens the young orator, though terrified, spoke boldly.
questions.answer: Athēnīs ōrātor iuvenis, quamquam perterritus, audācter dīxit.

questions.prompt: Born at Rome, the poet spent his old age at Baiae.
questions.answer: Rōmae nātus, poēta senectūtem Bāiīs ēgit.

questions.prompt: In war the brave leader, when the enemy had been conquered, was praised by all.
questions.answer: Bellī dux fortis, hostibus victīs, ab omnibus laudātus est.

questions.prompt: At Brundisium in the evening the prepared fleet awaited the signal.
questions.answer: Brundisiī vesperī classis parāta signum exspectābat.

questions.prompt: At Capua the exiled king, stripped of his kingdom, lay dying on the ground.
questions.answer: Capuae rēx exsul, rēgnō prīvātus, humī moriēbātur.

questions.prompt: At Tarentum the merchant, once his wares had been sold, gladly stayed at home.
questions.answer: Tarentī mercātor, mercibus vēnditīs, domī laetus mānsit.

questions.prompt: Yesterday at Delos the priest consulted the oracle about the war.
questions.answer: Herī Dēlī sacerdōs ōrāculum dē bellō cōnsuluit.

questions.prompt: In suspense of mind, the general at Corinth awaited the outcome of the battle.
questions.answer: Animī pendēns, dux Corinthī pugnae ēventum exspectābat.

questions.prompt: In war the fearless soldier scorned his wounds; at home he cultivated peace.
questions.answer: Bellī mīles intrepidus vulnera sprēvit; domī pācem coluit.

questions.prompt: At evening the weary shepherd, driving his flock, returned home.
questions.answer: Vesperī pāstor fessus, gregem agēns, domum rediit.

questions.prompt: In war and at home alike, the consul was judged wise.
questions.answer: Bellī et domī cōnsul sapiēns jūdicātus est.

questions.prompt: In military service the young man endured many hardships.
questions.answer: Mīlitiae adulēscēns multōs labōrēs perpessus est.

questions.prompt: At Miletus the philosopher used to teach that the soul is immortal.
questions.answer: Mīlētī philosophus animum immortālem esse docēbat.

questions.prompt: Lying on the ground, the captives at Pergamum kept begging for mercy.
questions.answer: Humī jacentēs, captīvī Pergamī veniam ōrābant.

questions.prompt: In suspense of mind at home, the father awaited his son's letter.
questions.answer: Animī domī pendēns, pater fīliī litterās exspectābat.

questions.prompt: At Antium the general, though brave in war, nevertheless seemed sad.
questions.answer: Antiī dux, bellī fortis, tamen trīstis vidēbātur.
